topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the lecture structure, learning outcomes, and the historical framework of cancer hallmarks centered on the loss of growth control.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Intracellular Signaling Cascades
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive sustained proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic alterations prevent cells from withdrawing from the cell cycle into terminally differentiated states across different tissue types.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptotic Cell Death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations impairing the p53 regulatory network and altering the balance of mitochondrial proteins allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit via telomerase activation while bypassing normal protective senescence and stress checkpoints.

topics.label: Deregulating Cellular Metabolism and Oncometabolite Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire metabolic pathways toward aerobic glycolysis and how metabolic enzyme mutations generate oncometabolites that perturb gene expression.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the requirement for new blood vessel recruitment to support tumor expansion and the regulatory balance governing the angiogenic switch.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Systemic Colonization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the multistep metastatic cascade, the clinical detection of disseminating tumor cells, and the factors enabling colonization at distant sites.

topics.label: Conclusion and Hallmarks Framework Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the overarching concepts of cancer hallmarks and concludes the lecture.
